## The Shanghai Composite dropped 0.7% to close at 3,966, while the Shenzhen Component fell 0.3% to 13,996 on Thursday, reversing gains from the previous session as markets reassessed the durability of a fragile US–Iran ceasefire. Tensions resurfaced after Israel launched its heaviest strikes yet on Lebanon, while Iran warned it may be “unreasonable” to proceed with talks on a permanent deal, raising doubts over the truce. Consumer staples and financial shares led declines, down 1.4% each. Other notable losses were seen from Foxconn Industrial (-2.8%), Zijin Mining (-2.1%), and BYD (-2.2%). Conversely, energy stocks edged higher as oil prices rebounded. Investors are now focused on China’s first-quarter inflation data due Friday, which is expected to offer clues on domestic demand. China is expected to emerge from deflation earlier than markets anticipate, with PPI, CPI, and the GDP deflator all projected to turn positive year-on-year in the first quarter.

## China's main stock market index, the SHANGHAI, fell to 3966 points on April 9, 2026, losing 0.72% from the previous session. Over the past month, the index has declined 3.81%, though it remains 23.03% higher than a year ago, according to trading on a contract for difference (CFD) that tracks this benchmark index from China. Historically, the China Shanghai Composite Stock Market Index reached an all time high of 6124.04 in October of 2007. - Securities Market

- Market capitalisation was $45.9 trillion at the end of March 2026, an increase of 15 per cent from $40.0 trillion for the same period last year.

- The average daily turnover in March 2026 was $304.0 billion, an increase of 8 per cent from $280.2 billion for the same period last year.

- The average daily turnover for the first three months of 2026 was $276.7 billion, an increase of 14 per cent when compared with $242.7 billion for the same period last year.

- The average daily turnover of derivative warrants for the first three months of 2026 was $7.5 billion, an increase of 1 per cent when compared with $7.4 billion for the same period last year.

- The average daily turnover of CBBCs for the first three months of 2026 was $13.9 billion, an increase of 40 per cent when compared with $9.9 billion for the same period last year.

- The average daily turnover of ETFs for the first three months of 2026 was $40.2 billion, an increase of 15 per cent when compared with $35.0 billion for the same period last year.

- The average daily turnover of L&I Products for the first three months of 2026 was $4.9 billion, an increase of 11 per cent when compared with $4.4 billion for the same period last year.

- There were 40 newly listed companies for the first three months of 2026, an increase of 135 per cent when compared with 17* for the same period last year.

- Funds raised through IPOs# for the first three months of 2026 was $109.9 billion, an increase of 488 per cent when compared with $18.7 billion for the same period last year.

- Total funds raised for the first three months of 2026 was $150.2 billion.

- Derivatives Market

- The average daily volume of futures and options for the first three months of 2026 was 1,828,560 contracts.

- The average daily volume of Stock Options for the first three months of 2026 was 943,511 contracts.

As of March 2025, the SSE Composite Index had closed at 3,335.75 points. The index reflects the performance of all stocks traded on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, including both boards, the main board, and the [Star market](/statistics/1140063/china-monthly-performance-of-the-star-50-index/).

## SSE still number one
In the greater Chinese region, the stock exchange in Shanghai was the largest, beating the bourses in Shenzhen, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. In 2023, the Shanghai Stock Exchange recorded a [market capitalization of over 6.5 trillion.](/statistics/234535/market-capitalization-of-capital-markets-in-greater-china-by-stock-exchange/)Not only market capitalization was a unique attribute, but the Shanghai Stock Exchange was also home to the most valuable stock in mainland China, which was the [baijiu producer Moutai Kweichow.](/statistics/1131569/china-kweichow-moutai-stock-annual-performance/)

## Limited access
Despite its size, the exchange in Shanghai only grants limited access to overseas investors. The bourse listed A-shares and B-shares. While A-shares are denominated in yuan and almost exclusively available for domestic traders, the prices of B-shares are in U.S. dollars and available for overseas investors as well. In addition, the bourse offers access to foreign investors through a trading accreditation which is supervised by the Chinese authorities. However, these tight controls are the reason why Hong Kong, despite its [lower relative market capitalization](/statistics/1301419/hong-kong-market-cap-of-hkex-by-trading-board/), remains an important gateway to capital for mainland Chinese companies.
